subject.title: fix(codex): backoff startup connection-close retries and surface exhaustion (#83959) [AI-assisted]

question: Should this PR land as the bounded backoff mitigation for Codex app-server startup-close exhaustion, or should maintainers require an explicit replacement-server readiness receipt first?
rationale: The patch is focused and proof-backed, but it deliberately changes startup failure timing and chooses bounded backoff over the readiness-gate shape suggested in the linked issue discussion.

options.title: Accept bounded backoff
options.body: Land this PR if the bounded five-attempt retry window is an acceptable mitigation for observed transient replacement-server warm-up failures.

options.title: Require readiness receipt
options.body: Ask for a follow-up revision that admits retries only after the replacement app-server proves it accepted a healthy initialize/request boundary.

options.title: Defer to broader startup lifecycle work
options.body: Pause this PR if maintainers want the shared-client eviction and startup readiness issues solved together rather than as a narrow mitigation.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded backoff
recommendation.body: Land this PR if the bounded five-attempt retry window is an acceptable mitigation for observed transient replacement-server warm-up failures.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the broadest ownership signal across Codex app-server startup, shared-client, binding-store, and turn-routing refactors.
